key_insight: A vorticity-augmented supervised model reconstructs turbulent flow fields most accurately at lower sparsity, while a physics-informed PINN is more robust when measurements become very sparse.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical path for compressing expensive turbulence data and recovering key flow statistics and structures from sparse sensors in CFD and experimental settings.
method: Supervised reconstruction with vorticity augmentation to better preserve turbulent structures.
Partially assisted compressible PINN using the 3D unsteady compressible Navier--Stokes equations.
Compare reconstruction quality across sparsity levels using field, spectral, and statistical metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on instantaneous velocity fields, mean-squared error, energy spectra, Reynolds stresses, turbulent kinetic energy, and Q-criterion isosurfaces across multiple sparsity levels.
watch_item: The supervised approach depends on high-resolution labels, and the PINN may be harder to train and less accurate than the supervised model at moderate sparsity.
paper_title: SCoReT: Super-Resolution Compression and Reconstruction of Turbulent Flows
